lead: you find out what you have agreed to from whoever is already thanking you for it. somebody told them a fortnight ago that you would sort it, and nobody rang you.
sun: by the time you know, the fastest way through is the one your hands were going to take anyway — the call made that evening, the name produced, the form done at the kitchen table before the week turns. the assumption is discharged before it could have been discussed, it goes off running under their arrangements, and being right about you costs the person who assumed exactly nothing.
moon: what makes it work is that nothing was entered into. there was no request and no agreement, no terms and no end, which leaves the whole of it unavailable for inspection by anybody, yourself included. after a few years it gets described as something you have always done. that is accurate. it is also why nobody wonders when it began.
pull: the person thanking you is the only one who ever put it to you, and by then it was a fact. that is how you learn what you are doing this month.
tension: the only person available to be put right is the one who did nothing wrong. she was told, she believed it, she has been grateful since tuesday. saying no means walking into her week and explaining that the man who promised on your behalf was talking about somebody nobody had consulted — which breaks her thing rather than yours. so you do it, and the next one gets arranged the same way, on better evidence.
cost: nothing has to be squared with you first, which is why so much of it exists — a plan with you in it needs no meeting and no fallback, and the thing gets started. the whole of it also lives outside language. no request, no agreement, nothing written, and therefore nothing with an exit in it, because an exit is a clause and there are no clauses.

lead: she asked you not to say anything, and you have not, and by the spring there was a job she could take in a town she happened to hear about. she has never put the two side by side.
sun: a thing told to you does not sit. within a week your hands have put something in the world that answers it — a word in the right ear, an arrangement made to look like weather, a door left ajar somewhere they were already going. you have repeated nothing. what you were told got out regardless, converted into conditions, carrying no trace of the sentence it came from.
moon: none of it was built from what she actually said. the ear takes the sentence underneath — the one being worked around, the one she has not yet put to herself — and that is the version your hands receive. so what turns up is shaped to a difficulty she never described, fits closer than anything she asked for, and is not explicable by anybody standing in the room.
pull: nothing anybody told you has ever been repeated, and every word of it was acted on. what you make for people fits because it answers the thing they were working around.
tension: the ones who work out that the timing was not luck go quiet on you afterwards. what would explain it is that you heard the part they were careful to leave out, heard it the first evening, and had acted on it by the weekend — and that lands as having been read rather than helped. so coincidence is the safest version, and the closest work you do for anyone is the part they must be kept from noticing.
cost: the polite account of the worst thing in somebody's life is enough for you to work from, and the conditions around it alter inside a season with nothing said aloud anywhere. receiving one and leaving it alone is the move you do not have. the hands discharge whatever the ear takes in, including the times when being heard and left alone was the whole of what was wanted.

lead: nothing that has happened around you in ten years was an occasion. it went out on a wednesday, the way it goes out every wednesday, at a size too small for anybody to remember receiving.
sun: the starting here comes as a rate rather than an event. two or three a week, for years: the suggestion made in passing, the introduction typed on a train, the half page sent to somebody who asked for nothing. each lands below the size at which a person registers being pushed, so no single one is memorable, and the sum of them is where the current motion around you came from.
moon: the beat is doing the work, and a beat has to be kept whether or not you have anything that week. people take their bearings off the frequency: they know roughly when they will hear from you, they arrange their weeks against it, and it has not occurred to any of them that it is a schedule. keeping in touch is the mechanism holding a dozen lives in phase.
pull: a decade of wednesdays, and nearly everything now running in the lives around you started in one of them. no single wednesday in that row is worth mentioning to anyone.
tension: the week something of your own actually matters, there is no register available for saying so. it goes out at the wednesday volume, in the wednesday shape, fourth in a row of five, because that is the only shape your output has, and it arrives looking like the rest of the traffic. people who would drop everything for you do not, and are not careless: the message indicated no difference, and indicating one is the instrument you were never issued.
cost: what goes out is small enough that nobody has to agree to anything, so it gets taken up without a decision anywhere, and ten years of that outruns any single project you might have run instead. the beat does not check whether you meant it. on the weeks with nothing in you, something goes out anyway, and it starts, and it is running now under somebody's name.

lead: come and stay has a date on it. it was said out loud, to one person, on an evening you could both put a month to, which makes it the only act of yours anybody can trace.
sun: the stay is when the making happens. by the second week there is an application in, a number to ring on thursday, somebody you know expecting them — and it is finished well before the stay is. they go out with their own thing already in motion, and what is in motion carries nothing of the house: no address, no debt, no reason to report back. the room held them while it got built.
moon: offering it took a sentence, said aloud, to one person, and it had to be accepted before anything followed. nothing else your hands do requires that. the rest leaves you with no visible moment of handover, so the receiver cannot say when it arrived. the bed can be dated exactly. it is the one piece of you that came into a life through the front door.
pull: everything your hands make leaves without a moment anybody could point at. the one act with a date and a witness is a bed, the smallest part of what happened to them.
tension: there is no sentence that closes it. come and stay was one clean act; the reverse is not an act at all, only a cooling, done by degrees, and readable as something having gone wrong with you personally. so the room goes on being available years past the point at which it did anybody good, and whoever stays longest in it is the one for whom none of the rest took.
cost: the small room has taken whoever needed it, at no notice, for eleven years, and each of them went out with something of their own that had begun in the third week. what you can produce, asked what the life has come to, is a number of beds — countable, dateable, the one figure available to you, and the least interesting fact about any of them.
